title: Speed Webb's band: arrangers and why it never came to New York
summary: Speed Webb only fronted; the band included Gus Wilson, Teddy Wilson, Jonesy and others, wrote all night, never recorded, and the leader avoided New York.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: ...go back to Speed Webb. You said it was a very good band and that the mistake they made was that they never came to New York.

Well, not that they made. It was the leader. He wouldn't ever bring us to New York, you know. The closest we got to New York was Boston, and we went from Boston (oh boy!) in a raggedy bus all the ways to Woonsocket, Wisconsin. And we was about ten minutes late. We got there and the man had hired a local band. The place was like this. That local band wouldn't let us play.
Did Speed Webb say he'd been to Hollywood? Because he spent some time out there.

Oh, he'd been to Hollywood. Yeah, that was after that. He had been there, and he had pictures of him where he was in a movie or something, you know... I guess he was a drummer of some sort(?), you know.
Did he play drums with the band?
No.
He just fronted it.
He just...
Conducted.
Conductor, yeah.
I was curious about Teddy's brother, Gus. He was in that band, wasn't he?
Eldridge - 46
Yeah. Great arranger, man. Great arranger. Really great. Great trombone player, too.
He died young, didn't he?
I didn't realize he was dead. Who told you he was dead?
I don't know. I always thought, because he kind of disappeared...
Well, he did disappear, but I don't think he's dead, though. I don't know, to tell you the truth.
[PAUSE]
I hadn't seen him in years, since he left the band, you know. I don't know what happened.
Teddy was writing, too, wasn't he?

Yeah. Teddy, Jonesy, Chuck Lawless(?), Leonard Day... It was a good band. We'd take turns on sleeping. Cats would write all night, then we'd rehearse and...all day. And we (?) that we was ready. Didn't do any rehearsing.
Never got to make any records, huh?
No.
Was he just a bad businessman, or was he afraid that somebody would raid the band or something?
No, he just liked to be... You know, like a cat gets to be where he's a big shot, you know... Like, in
Eldridge - 47

Indianapolis, you know, he had a lot of chicks there, you know. He had an ego problem going. And there he was big, you know. I guess he didn't want to hit New York, where he may get snuffed out, heh-heh. But he didn't even come in.
